metadata.title: Conceptual inconsistencies in finite-dimensional quantum and classical mechanics

extraction_notes.note: Numbered equations (1) and (5)-(6) retyped as external theorems because the text names them as results (Weyl's demonstration; the Ehrenfest theorems).
definition or remark: the sentence both asserts that the eigenbases are mutually unbiased and explains the term; kept as an external definition.

Eqs. (7)-(8) and (15) are derived in prose by applying ODM to the Ehrenfest theorems, but the derivation sentence contains the equation and an equation is not a result, so no proof node was made; the dependency is recorded as uses edges from the Ehrenfest theorems and ODM.
One sentence introduces two symbols (H_mub^star and H_mub); a sentence cannot be split, so one definition node carries both.
The numerical evidence (spectra and twentieth eigenvectors) is only in the figures, whose content is not extractable; the claims rest on them.
The Introduction's and Outlook's summary sentences restating the paper's findings, and the numerical parameter-selection recipe, were left out as non-statement discussion.

\label{NoFreeFiniteDimQM_Theorem}
	Assume $\hat{p}$ and $\hat{H}$ are non-zero finite-dimensional Hermitian operators. If $\commut{ \hat{H}, \hat{p} } = 0$ then there is no finite-dimensional linear operator $\hat{x}$ such that $i \commut{ \hat{H}, \hat{x} } = \hat{p}$.

nodes.statement: Let ketE_n denote a joint eigenvector of hatH and hatp such that hatH ketE_n = E_n ketE_n and hatp ketE_n = p_n ketE_n. Assuming that i commut hatH, hatx = hatp, one obtains i braE_n commut hatH, hatx ketE_m = i (E_n - E_m) braE_n hatx ketE_m = p_m langle E_n ketE_m, forall n,m. The special case of this identity, when n=m, reads p_m = 0, forall m. This contradicts the assumption that hatp is a non-zero matrix.
